title: Converge delimiter silhouettes and runtime fallbacks for chat onboarding
creator: Miguel Rivera
description: Background: New model variants arriving from community forks exhibit subtle differences in role/assistant delimiters and subtokenization behavior. We've seen two classes of customer regressions during onboarding: (1) role markers (e.g., "Assistant:" vs "Assistant:\n") producing shifted token counts that invalidate latency/throughput expectations, and (2) boundary subtokens that split template placeholders leading to malformed structured outputs. This ticket standardizes a lightweight compatibility layer that normalizes delimiter 'silhouettes' at onboarding time, records an explicit tokenizer compatibility tag in the published performance profile, and wires runtime fallbacks for older/pinned versions.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline emits a tokenizer_compatibility tag (string) in the model's performance profile whenever automatic normalization is applied

A compatibility shim normalizes at least the top 6 delimiter variants we observe in dataset (role prefixes, trailing newlines, colon/no-colon, angle-bracket role markers) without changing model weights
Runtime applies an automatic, opt-out fallback to a compatible template variant when an incoming prompt triggers a delimiter mismatch at inference time
Regression suite (unit + integration) includes 18 fuzz cases covering common subtoken boundaries and passes in CI for runtime-1.22
Docs and onboarding checklist updated with clear guidance for version pinning and when to request a tokenizer re-roll
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Add model variant with template using 'Assistant: ' delimiter and publish without normalization

2) Send chat messages that use 'Assistant:
' and observe token counts differ by >5% on tokenized length leading to unexpected batching behavior
3) Send structured output prompts where "<item>" splits into subtokens and assert that parser fails to extract the placeholder
4) Observe no tokenizer_compatibility tag in published performance profile and no runtime fallback triggered
implementation_notes: - Build a small, reversible normalization layer: canonicalize delimiters to a canonical token sequence mapping; do not mutate model weights or vocab files during onboarding
- Emit a tokenizer_compatibility string in the model metadata (e.g., 'redwood:tok_compat:v1') that the console + API can surface; include normalized_examples sample

- Add an inference-time detector that checks tokenized roles against the model's declared silhouette and, if mismatch and latency budget allows, rewrites the prompt using the compatibility mapping and records a fallback event in tracing
- Keep normalization opt-out: allow model owners to disable via onboarding flag so advanced users can keep raw tokenizer behavior for research models
- Add fast C++/Rust tokenizer helper used by runtime and onboarding worker to avoid Python overhead; include fuzz tests to cover subtoken edges
- Performance trade-off: normalization adds ~0.2ms median overhead on short prompts but prevents costly batching anomalies and structured-output failures; benchmark data attached
- Coordinate with model catalog team to ensure performance profile publishing includes token-count distributions before and after normalization

2025-02-26 QA: Integration tests show 0.2–0.5ms median extra latency on 1–3 token prompts, but eliminates 100% of observed parsing failures in our test corpus. Marking as worth the trade-off.
